The three-peat is on. No woman has won 3 consecutive US Opens since Serena Williams in 2014.

#USOpen #Tennis #WTA #Sabalenka

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Sabalenka took just 75 minutes to dispatch Wimbledon champion Noskova today.

14 winners. 2 breaks per set. Zero drama.

She's coming for a third straight US Open title. 👀 #USOpen #Tennis #WTA #Sabalenka

facebook.long_form:
Aryna Sabalenka moved one step closer to making history on Tuesday morning at the US Open, defeating Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-4, 6-3 in just 75 minutes.

The performance was typically dominant. Sabalenka hit 14 winners, broke Noskova twice in each set, and never looked threatened. It was the kind of focused, methodical tennis that has made her the best player on the planet this season. 🎾

The numbers that matter most: no woman has won three consecutive US Open titles since Serena Williams completed the feat in 2014. Sabalenka won in 2024 and 2025. She's now two wins away from doing it again.

Her next opponent comes from the Gauff/Andreeva quarterfinal playing later today. Either way, it promises to be a semifinal worth staying up for.

Do you think Sabalenka's three-peat is inevitable at this point, or can someone stop her?

---

stories.title: All-American QF — Tiafoe vs. Michelsen at 1 PM ET (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
TODAY: Frances Tiafoe vs. Alex Michelsen — 1 PM ET, Louis Armstrong Stadium.

A U.S. man is GUARANTEED in the US Open semifinals for the first time since Andy Roddick in 2003.

#USOpen #Tennis #ATP #AmericanTennis

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Tiafoe (26, 11th seed) vs. Michelsen (22, unseeded).

One will make US Open history for American men. The drought since Roddick in 2003 ends today.

Tune in: 1 PM ET on ESPN. #USOpen #Tennis #ATP #Tiafoe

facebook.long_form:
Here's something American tennis fans haven't been able to say in 23 years: a U.S. man is guaranteed to be in the US Open semifinals. 🇺🇸

Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen play each other today at 1 PM ET at Louis Armstrong Stadium — and whoever wins makes history. The drought since Andy Roddick won the last US Open for American men in 2003 is officially over. The question now is who carries the flag into the final four.

Tiafoe (11th seed, 26 years old) has been here before, reaching the semis in 2022. He beat Daniil Medvedev in four sets to get here. Michelsen is unseeded and just 22 — he dismissed Tomas Etcheverry in straight sets without drama.

Two American kids. One historic opportunity. Tuesday at 1 PM ET on ESPN.

Who are you rooting for — Tiafoe or Michelsen?

---

stories.title: Gauff vs. Andreeva — Defending Champ Eyes Semis Return (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Coco Gauff vs. Mirra Andreeva in the US Open QFs tonight at Arthur Ashe.

Both 21 years old. Andreeva beat Gauff at the 2026 French Open SF. Gauff is the 2023 US Open champion.

Rematch. Same stakes. #USOpen #Tennis #WTA #Gauff

facebook.long_form:
Two 21-year-olds who are already shaping the future of women's tennis. Tonight at Arthur Ashe Stadium, Coco Gauff and Mirra Andreeva meet in the quarterfinals of the US Open — and the stakes don't get much higher. 🎾

Gauff is the 2023 US Open champion, determined to get back to the final. Andreeva is the 2026 French Open champion, one of the most complete players on tour right now. Earlier this year, Andreeva beat Gauff in the French Open semifinals. Tonight is the rematch.

The winner faces Sabalenka in the semis — who shut down Wimbledon champion Noskova this morning in just 75 minutes. The path to the final runs through two giants.

Arthur Ashe, evening session. This is must-watch tennis.

Who wins this one — Gauff or Andreeva?

---

stories.title: Alcaraz vs. Shelton — Night Session Arthur Ashe (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Carlos Alcaraz vs. Ben Shelton — TONIGHT at Arthur Ashe, approx. 8 PM ET.

Alcaraz leads H2H 3-0. But Shelton didn't face a single break point vs. Tsitsipas.

New York's crowd is loud and it's in Shelton's corner. #USOpen #Tennis #ATP #Alcaraz

facebook.long_form:
The night session at Arthur Ashe tonight features one of the most compelling storylines of the entire US Open: Carlos Alcaraz — the No. 2 seed returning from 139 days off after a wrist injury — against Ben Shelton, the big-serving American showman who is New York's adopted son. 🌙

Alcaraz leads their head-to-head 3-0. But this isn't 2024 Shelton. He demolished Stefanos Tsitsipas in the fourth round 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 without facing a single break point. His serve is working at a frightening level. The Arthur Ashe crowd is going to be thunderous for him.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, has looked a little tentative at times — understandable for someone just two tournaments removed from surgery. But when he's locked in, he's capable of beating anyone.

This one could go five sets. Get comfortable. 📺 Approx. 8 PM ET.

Which storyline do you believe in tonight — Shelton's home crowd energy or Alcaraz's pedigree?

---

stories.title: QF Day 2 Preview — Zverev, Pegula, Navarro, Van de Zandschulp (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Wednesday at the US Open:

🎾 Zverev vs. Van de Zandschulp
🎾 Pegula vs. Navarro (Navarro won this matchup at the 2024 US Open)

Plus the night session winner of Alcaraz/Shelton on the men's side.

#USOpen #Tennis #ATP #WTA

facebook.long_form:
After today's packed QF slate, Wednesday brings the other half of the draw — and it's stacked. 📅

In the men's side, defending champion Alexander Zverev (No. 1 seed) takes on Botic van de Zandschulp, a Dutch player who Zverev says might love the US Open more than any tournament on tour. Zverev is the favorite but Van de Zandschulp has been relentless.

In the women's side, No. 3 Jessica Pegula squares off against No. 26 Emma Navarro in an all-American showdown. Navarro beat Pegula at the 2024 US Open en route to the semis. Pegula will be looking for revenge — and Navarro will be looking for her first Grand Slam final.

Either way, an American woman is guaranteed to be in the US Open semifinals on Wednesday.

Two huge matches. Wednesday at Flushing Meadows. Who's watching?

---
